SC-2: One assessment tuple (source, control, sink, path, boundary, counterevidence, proof gaps) after a surface and source-trust class step.
SC-3: A credential in any source file is a disclosure path, judged by format and use, never tested, described by key and location; public keys and placeholders are not findings.

taken.mechanism: SC-5: Triage supplied findings as confirmed, not-actionable (positive evidence on every shipped path) or needs-review (the smallest missing fact); rank by exploitability, scanner severity last.
SC-6: Snippets labelled by role, checked against the cited lines.
SC-7: Attack your own patch before verifying it; verify on the original attack path; an empty rescan, a closed ticket or renamed code is not proof.
SC-9: Publication is idempotent (id and fingerprint in every item, search before create, settle an ambiguous write by reading) and private by default.
SC-11: A prior dismissal holds only while its stated reason still holds against current source; a bare false-positive label never dismisses.
SC-12: Finding identity is rule family, root-control anchor without line numbers, and an instance key per attackable sibling; group only on matching control and fix.
SC-13: The scope receipt is the revision for a clean checkout, else a digest including staged and untracked files, never with remote-URL credentials.
SC-14: The report is generated by code from the validated record; the agent never edits it.
SC-15: Vulnerable and fixed commit pairs test the skill, labels in harness metadata only.
SC-16: Stop discovery reruns after N runs add nothing new, or at a run or time cap; a resume keeps the limit.
